key_insight: SplashSplat introduces the first synchronized multi-view benchmark for real-world splashing liquids, enabling researchers to study and reconstruct a highly dynamic phenomenon that was previously missing from evaluation datasets. It shows that splashes can now be captured and benchmarked across multiple views, despite their fleeting, textureless, and view-dependent nature.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of real-world, synchronized multi-view data for splashing liquids, which has made it difficult to evaluate and advance reconstruction methods for fast, chaotic fluid events.
method: Collects a benchmark of 20 real splash scenes, ranging from coherent liquid streams to violent splashes.
Captures each scene with seven synchronized cameras to provide multi-view observations of rapid fluid motion.
Focuses on evaluation by providing a challenging dataset that reflects the true appearance and dynamics of splashing liquids.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark fills a major gap in reconstruction research and provides a realistic testbed for developing methods that handle transient, non-rigid, and view-dependent phenomena. It can help improve robustness in 3D reconstruction, vision, and simulation pipelines for fluids and other fast-moving materials.

paper_title: SplashSplat: Reconstructing Splashing Liquids from Real-World Multi-View Videos
paper_authors: Peiyu Liu, Dingxi Zhang, Federico Tombari, Marc Pollefeys, Christina Tsalicoglou
